title: Show the sequence, don't claim it
statement: Check a claimed knowledge sequence by working through the delivered lessons: the pre-teaching, the link and the deeper revisit must be visible, or the claim doesn't count.
example: One course claimed 3 compounding threads across its texts; working through the lessons showed no link, no pre-teaching and no revisit.
detail: One reading course claimed 3 compounding threads across its texts; working through the lessons showed two unrelated texts with no link, no pre-teaching and no revisit (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`). The course evaluation criteria require knowledge sequencing to be observable in the app, as pre-teaching, a visible link to the passage and a revisit at greater depth, and say claims that can't be seen by clicking through do not count (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/timeback-course-eval/references/eval-criteria.md`). The evaluation gauntlet's knowledge-sequence probe picks a lesson and asks whether what it assumes was taught earlier and whether anything is revisited at greater depth later (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/train-teacher/references/gauntlet-spec.md`).

evidence.quote: with no link, no pre-teach, no revisit
claims that aren't observable don't count
**Knowledge sequencing is observable in-app** — pre-teach → visible passage linkage → revisit at greater depth. Claims that can't be seen by clicking through do not count.
**Knowledge-sequence probe**: pick a lesson; is what it assumes taught earlier? Is anything revisited at greater depth later? (Observable, click-through standard.)

Four ladder claims in our older design documents were found to cite content Grade 3 does not actually teach; all four are corrected in the data, and the swap that removed Human Body II also removed the one true same-depth repeat.
**The plan can promise observable compounding; only the built lessons can prove it.**
